answer: Memory-hard registration resists sybils: minting an identity requires solving a puzzle (Argon2/scrypt-style) that must hold a large block of RAM for its whole run — cheap to verify, impossible to shrink. GPUs cannot mirror the work cheaply, since each concurrent solve needs its own canyon of memory, so a farm is capped by total RAM, not core count. An honest agent pays one cedar-solid memory puzzle once; an operator minting a thousand keys in parallel must buy a thousandfold memory, turning cheap mass registration into a hardware-bound cost wall.
